rows.contract: Match Action::Exec dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The controller action exec <cmd> runs nothing itself: it returns an exec effect carrying the command and the config's child environment, and the shell runs /bin/sh -c <cmd> with posix_spawn, detached in a session of its own with standard input and output on /dev/null, never waiting on the main loop. Reachable from a key or mouse binding in the config file and as msg action exec <cmd> over the IPC socket; fixture modes ignore the effect. Known mismatches: upstream's five Wayland toolkit environment fallbacks are withheld unless the file's [env] sets them; the cursor is not revealed; any same-user process that can write to the socket can have the app run a command, as with upstream's msg action exec. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (the effect, not the process), and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode, in which an exec'd command wrote its environment to a file, left no saved evidence; a key or mouse binding firing it is unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: The controller action spawn <cmd> returns the same exec effect as exec <cmd>, which the shell runs as /bin/sh -c <cmd>, detached. Unlike exec it is repeatable, as upstream: a hot key bound to it fires again while held, after input.keyboard.repeat_delay and then repeat_rate times a second. Reachable from a key or mouse binding in the config file and as msg action spawn <cmd>. Known mismatches: as for exec (Wayland toolkit environment fallbacks withheld, no cursor reveal, the socket lets a same-user process run a command); upstream's default spawn bindings (swaylock, wpctl, brightnessctl, playerctl, grim) name Linux programs that sh will not find on a Mac, and those on media keys are not registered at all. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (the effect, not the process), and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode, in which spawn touch <file> created the file, left no saved evidence; a key binding firing it and its repeat are unrun on a live run. rows.implementation_note: Camera-only controller go-to-bookmark <name>, parsed by the upstream action grammar, animates the output's camera so its usable-area centre lands on the stored canvas point, leaves zoom untouched and clears the output's Fit return. Default shell: the config file's bindings of go-to-bookmark <name> (upstream's defaults mod+1 to mod+4, Control-Option-1 to 4 under the default super chord), with a status-line hint when the bookmark does not exist; also reachable as msg action go-to-bookmark <name>. Known mismatches: no fullscreen interaction (Infinify has no fullscreen yet). No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios, and shortcut delivery, the Unix-socket path and rendered animation are unverified on a live run. rows.contract: Match Action::SetBookmark dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Camera-only controller set-bookmark <name> stores, as a centre point with Y up, the canvas point under the output's usable-area centre, computed as upstream does from the pending camera target, else the camera, and the current zoom: that is the destination of a camera-only flight (pan-viewport, go-to-bookmark, an IPC camera write), but an anchored zoom flight (home toggle, zoom step, fit, their returns, an IPC zoom write, window navigation) drops its camera target on its first tick, so a bookmark set during one captures the point under the usable-area centre at that moment (before that tick, the camera target paired with the zoom not yet changed), which is the flight's destination only by coincidence. It replaces any bookmark of that name in the live registry and reports the scene dirty; zoom is never stored. The registry is written to the scene file only with session.restore_bookmarks = true: with upstream's default (false) a bookmark set at runtime lasts until quit, and a save carries the file's earlier bookmarks forward untouched. Default shell: the config file's bindings of set-bookmark <name> (upstream's defaults mod+shift+1 to mod+shift+4, Control-Option-Shift-1 to 4 under the default super chord) with a Bookmark saved status line; also reachable as msg action set-bookmark <name> and msg bookmark <name> <x> <y>. Known mismatches: a scene file that contains bookmarks cannot be read by older builds. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios, and shortcut delivery, the Unix-socket path and a live scene save are unverified. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Action::ReloadConfig dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The controller action reload-config returns a reload_config effect; the shell sends load_config again, re-reads the bindings, re-registers its hot keys and refreshes the status line, tooltips and Quit title. The shell also reloads on its own when the config file changes (vnode watch on the file and its directory, 150 ms debounce). The controller follows upstream's reload: a file that cannot be read or parsed keeps the configuration in force and reports upstream's message, an accepted one replaces it whole, and config bookmarks are reconciled with the live registry (added or changed names re-asserted, removed names dropped, untouched names left at their runtime value). No default binding; reachable from a binding in the config file and as msg action reload-config. A file that goes missing after it was accepted is such a read failure: the configuration and the bookmark registry stay. Known mismatches: the shell's file watch also reloads when the file is deleted and so reports that read failure at once, where upstream's watcher ignores a deleted file; a reload while no file has been accepted yet reports no error for a missing file, where upstream reports a read failure; only the settings applied here are re-applied, since no keyboard layout, cursor theme, device, output rule or render cache exists to rebuild. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios, and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode (a file created, edited, broken, and moved away and back while running, and reload-config repeating a load) left no saved evidence; hot-key re-registration and the refreshed status line and tooltips are unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Reported by the bindings command. In both modes the shell registers a binding on the key that types its character in the current keyboard layout (TIS/UCKeyTranslate; unshifted, or with Shift for a binding that holds Shift) and resolves again when the input source changes, as upstream matches the active layout's keysym first. True, upstream's default: when no key types the character the binding falls back to its US ANSI key position. False: it is left out and noted. A key the layout resolves takes its chord before one that fell back. Known mismatches: the true fallback is the US ANSI position, where upstream falls back to the key's Latin keysym from another configured layout; with the flag false a binding that holds Shift is still found on the key that types its character without Shift, where upstream finds it there only through the fallback; only unshifted US-ANSI characters and named keys are bindable, and a symbol that needs Shift or another layout is reported as skipped. No evidence entry is recorded yet: the controller side is covered by exported-C-ABI/JSON scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/config_flow.rs); the shell's lookup was run only outside the app, linked into a scratch harness against the installed US, British, German, French, Dvorak and Russian layout tables with nothing registered, and hot-key registration, a key press on a non-US layout and an input-source change are unrun on a live run.
